questiontext.text:
[[if test="is(ix=1)"]]

A school farm made a profit of Ksh \(28\,000\). The profit is shared among the Agriculture, Environment and Science clubs in the ratio \(3 : 5 : 6\). Find each share.

[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=2)"]]

A school has \(600\) new exercise books to share among classes 12A, 12B and 12C in the ratio \(4 : 7 : 9\). Find each share.

[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=3)"]]

A co-operative shares \(1440\) kg of fertiliser among three farmers, Mutiso, Langat and Adhiambo, in the ratio \(2 : 5 : 11\). Find each share.

[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=4)"]]

A chama pays a dividend of Ksh \(45\,000\) to three members, Halima, Gitau and Ruto, in the ratio \(3 : 7 : 10\). Find each share.

[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=5)"]]

The county forest office gives \(720\) tree seedlings to Tumaini, Upendo and Mwangaza schools in the ratio \(5 : 6 : 9\). Find each share.

[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=6)"]]

A matatu SACCO pays a bonus of Ksh \(72\,000\) to three drivers, Kamau, Odhiambo and Kipkemoi, in the ratio \(6 : 7 : 11\). Find each share.

[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=7)"]]

A dairy gives \(480\) litres of milk for school feeding to Amani, Baraka and Neema schools in the ratio \(3 : 4 : 9\). Find each share.

[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=8)"]]

Three siblings, Wanjiku, Njoroge and Muthoni, share Ksh \(33\,000\) from the family's bean harvest in the ratio \(5 : 8 : 9\). Find each share.

[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=9)"]]

A school shares \(900\) new textbooks among its Grade 10, Grade 11 and Grade 12 classes in the ratio \(3 : 8 : 9\). Find each share.

[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=10)"]]

A school fundraiser made Ksh \(52\,000\). It is shared among the Drama, Music and Football clubs in the ratio \(4 : 9 : 13\). Find each share.

[[/if]]

generalfeedback.text:
Find one part first, then each share is a number of parts.

Total number of parts: \({@a@} + {@b@} + {@c@} = {@S@}\).

One part: \({@ksh(P)@} \div {@S@} = {@ksh(one)@}\).

Shares: \({@a@} \times {@ksh(one)@} = {@ksh(s1)@}\), \({@b@} \times {@ksh(one)@} = {@ksh(s2)@}\) and \({@c@} \times {@ksh(one)@} = {@ksh(s3)@}\).

Check: \({@ksh(s1)@} + {@ksh(s2)@} + {@ksh(s3)@} = {@ksh(P)@}\).

questiondescription.text:
Compound Proportions: sharing in a three-part ratio

Grade 12 CBE Core 1.3 / Essential 1.2 (a): Share a quantity in a three-part ratio.

Core and Essential

This question is adapted from Chapter 17 (Ratio), Section C, question C6 of Ling, J., Scruton, P., Shilton, S. and West, H., SMP GCSE Mathematics: Foundation 2 for AQA, Edexcel and OCR two-tier GCSE mathematics, Cambridge University Press, 2007: new ratios, totals and Kenyan contexts.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Core and Essential Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).

truefeedback.text: That is an equal share. In the ratio \({@a@} : {@b@} : {@c@}\) the shares are different: find one part first.
You divided by \(3\), the number of people. Divide by the total number of parts, \({@a@} + {@b@} + {@c@} = {@S@}\).
